paths.description: Public root and only discoverable page archetype. Audited because the response exposed no links, sitemap entries, application routes, forms, or content templates. Not covered: authenticated or undisclosed routes, because none were linked or listed and no source was supplied.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Dark-mode screenshot remains a blank white viewport and the computed color-scheme is normal; the server ships no authored UI or theme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide authored surface colors that adapt through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: The blank document exposes no state, route, control, or primary interaction, so there is no natural transition or usable interaction feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the empty response with a valid authored HTML document and semantic content.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: The blank document has zero links, headings, landmarks, or controls and provides no orientation or attention guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the empty response with a valid authored HTML document and semantic content.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: The screenshot and DOM show zero content, so content is not being prioritized or presented at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the empty response with a valid authored HTML document and semantic content.

findings.summary: Layout adapts to narrow viewports with no horizontal overflow and no fixed pixel widths forcing a desktop layout on mobile; viewport meta present; fluid scaling and intrinsic sizing rather than brittle breakpoints.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout metrics report no viewport meta and a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport scaled to 0.367.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid mobile viewport and semantic, legible page structure that reflows at narrow widths.

findings.summary: The page communicates what it is for and exposes the primary next action without requiring users to hunt through decorative content, generic copy, or competing calls to action.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains an empty body, zero links, zero forms, no title, no main content, and no action or recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful HTML that states the site purpose, presents a clear primary action, and includes visible empty/error recovery states.

findings.summary: The representative primary flow can be completed end-to-end with predictable steps, no avoidable dead ends, no hidden required information, and no needless detours through modals, account walls, or upsells.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains an empty body, zero links, zero forms, no title, no main content, and no action or recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful HTML that states the site purpose, presents a clear primary action, and includes visible empty/error recovery states.

findings.summary: Loading, empty, success, error, offline, and partial-completion states are visible and actionable; users can retry, undo, cancel, go back, or continue without losing context.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains an empty body, zero links, zero forms, no title, no main content, and no action or recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful HTML that states the site purpose, presents a clear primary action, and includes visible empty/error recovery states.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse terminated with NO_FCP and the trace reports FCP and LCP as null because the page never paints content.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve paintable main content in the initial HTML so FCP and LCP can occur and be measured.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found no headings, landmarks, or focusable controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid mobile viewport and semantic, legible page structure that reflows at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Text is legible and inclusively rendered: comfortable line layout, precise alignment, stable rendering across mixed fonts, no clipping or cramped wrapping that harms comprehension.
findings.evidence: Rendered body contains zero text characters, so there is no legible or comparable content experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid mobile viewport and semantic, legible page structure that reflows at narrow widths.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: The document has no viewport meta; Chrome uses a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport at a requested 360-pixel device width.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid mobile viewport and semantic, legible page structure that reflows at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: DOM probe found no authored doctype, no declared charset, and Chrome fell back to windows-1252.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the empty response with a valid authored HTML document and semantic content.

findings.summary: The page has a unique, descriptive <title> and a meta description.
findings.evidence: Raw and rendered inspections show an empty title and no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add authored HTML with a descriptive title, meta description, viewport, canonical, crawlable navigation, valid robots.txt/sitemap.xml, and share metadata.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: DOM has zero links and no viewport meta; robots.txt returns the literal body "empty OK" rather than robots directives.
findings.suggestedFix: Add authored HTML with a descriptive title, meta description, viewport, canonical, crawlable navigation, valid robots.txt/sitemap.xml, and share metadata.

findings.summary: Public pages expose the indexing signals search engines need: successful HTTP status, canonical URL when appropriate, hreflang for localized variants, robots/sitemap consistency, and no accidental noindex/noarchive policy.
findings.evidence: The root is HTTP 200 but has no canonical, robots meta, hreflang, or content; sitemap.xml returns "empty OK" rather than XML.
findings.suggestedFix: Add authored HTML with a descriptive title, meta description, viewport, canonical, crawlable navigation, valid robots.txt/sitemap.xml, and share metadata.

findings.summary: Where the page represents an article, product, organization, event, place or other rich entity, structured data and share-preview metadata accurately describe the visible content.
findings.evidence: No visible entity, Open Graph tags, social card metadata, JSON-LD, or microdata exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add authored HTML with a descriptive title, meta description, viewport, canonical, crawlable navigation, valid robots.txt/sitemap.xml, and share metadata.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but curl shows HSTS max-age=1 and no CSP, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; the CDP header probe likewise reports those defenses absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a durable HSTS policy, CSP with frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a restrictive Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: Root response lacks CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; HSTS is only max-age=1.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a durable HSTS policy, CSP with frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a restrictive Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content and primary flows are reachable and usable without JavaScript and on older or non-Baseline browsers; modern features layer on as enhancements with fallbacks, and reactive/transition state stabilises rather than flickering before it settles.
findings.evidence: Raw fetch and JavaScript-enabled render both receive zero bytes of authored HTML and expose no core content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the empty response with a valid authored HTML document and semantic content.

findings.summary: HTTP errors, network failures, timeouts and stale data states are handled intentionally: users see useful recovery options rather than blank screens, infinite spinners, broken shells, or misleading success states.
findings.evidence: The server returns a blank HTTP 200 response with no useful error, retry, fallback, or recovery UI; robots and sitemap similarly return placeholder "empty OK" bodies.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the empty response with a valid authored HTML document and semantic content.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: The rendered html element has no lang or dir attribute; there is no authored CSS or translation-ready content.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare the document language and direction, then use logical CSS properties.
